name: Keisha Morgan

five_sec.what_is_it: A recipe-saver app with meal plans and a grocery list
five_sec.who_for: Super-organized people who already have a recipe collection
five_sec.trust_why: 4.8 App Store and 'no card required' right up top, but nothing about kids yet
five_sec.next_step: Scroll to see if I can mark what one person will and won't eat
five_sec.delivers_food_why: App Store badges and 'Recipes, Meal Plans and Grocery Lists, All in One App'; clearly just an app

full_page.what_stopped_me: It's a really nice binder, but I'm still the one doing all the safe-food math every night; nothing on the page plans around Jalen
full_page.whats_missing: Anything about different people at the table eating different things; which grocery stores the 'Deliver Groceries' button actually works with (is Kroger one?)

PTE.quote: Cute aisle-by-aisle list, but 'Meal Plans Tailored to Your Life' still means I'm the one tailoring every plan around Jalen's dozen safe foods.

five_sec.what_is_it: Meal kit boxes, with a 'pick a box' prize game
five_sec.who_for: People who like cooking new adventurous stuff and have money
five_sec.trust_why: First thing I see is 'Open A Box To Reveal Your Offer!' which is a carnival game, not information
five_sec.next_step: Tap 'Continue Without Offer' and probably leave
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Green HelloFresh boxes in the pop-up and '10 Free Meals' in the bottom bar

full_page.what_stopped_me: Every dish has a sauce or a mixed texture: gochujang aioli, pickled cabbage, pico, crema. Jalen can't sit next to half of it, and I can't lock his exact nuggets brand into a box
full_page.whats_missing: Price (it wants a zip first), any way to make one component plain for one kid

HF.quote: 'Kid-tested recipes' next to Bee Sting Hot Honey Pepperoni Pizzas. My kid runs exactly one test: is it the Perdue dino nugget. Hard pass.

five_sec.what_is_it: Plans the week's dinners, texts everyone in the house to vote, then drops the list into Instacart or Walmart
five_sec.who_for: Busy families with kids who argue about dinner
five_sec.trust_why: Plain and honest ('We don't deliver food'), but nothing on the first screen says it understands a kid like mine
five_sec.next_step: Tap 'See a sample week' to check whether the food is all casseroles
five_sec.delivers_food_why: The bold green line literally says 'We don't deliver food. We plan your week and send your grocery list.'

full_page.what_stopped_me: 'Familiar flavors, one safe thing on every plate' is word-for-word what Jalen's OT told me to do, and the Family profile has 'kid-safe foods'. Then Wednesday is 'Creamy Tomato Pasta with Hidden Veggies', which is the exact thing we don't do. Also the Kroger cart is Family-only, and it never says whether my exact brands stay in the cart or get swapped
full_page.whats_missing: A screenshot of one person's profile (won't-eats, safe foods); a line saying brands won't be swapped without asking; the words ARFID or sensory anywhere. I did notice Kroger is listed under Instacart stores, so maybe I don't need the paid Kroger push

DD.quote: 'One safe thing on every plate' — okay, somebody gets it. Then Wednesday is 'Hidden Veggies' pasta and I'm like… which one is it, Sarah?

five_sec.what_is_it: A weekly meal plan subscription with a video
five_sec.who_for: Moms who want new recipes every week
five_sec.trust_why: Looks like it's been around forever, real company, but generic happy-kid stock vibes
five_sec.delivers_food_why: 'Less Stress, More Dinners' over a kid laughing in a kitchen; could be a box, could be recipes

full_page.what_stopped_me: The Kid Friendly plan says 'Easy meals even the pickiest eaters will love'. That sentence is the lie every app tells me. No per-person anything, and a pop-up wanting my email before it'll show a price
full_page.whats_missing: Per-person won't-eats; price on the page; any acknowledgement that some kids don't 'try a bite'

EM.quote: 'Even the pickiest eaters will love' — ma'am, my son has ARFID. He is not going to love your Slow Cooker plan.

five_sec.what_is_it: An AI app that decides what's for dinner for you
five_sec.who_for: Parents carrying the dinner mental load
five_sec.trust_why: 'Trusted by 90,000+ families' and the headline is basically my life, but the big button is a 'Letter from the CEO', which is weird
five_sec.next_step: Scroll for reviews and how it works
five_sec.delivers_food_why: It's a phone mockup of a menu with notification bubbles; reads as an app

full_page.what_stopped_me: Price is a mess: the FAQ says a free month and 'prices are available when you download the app', the pricing page says $25 a month for 'messages'. And nothing about one kid eating a different plate
full_page.whats_missing: Per-person safe foods; Kroger (only Instacart, Walmart, Amazon Fresh listed); a straight price

OL.quote: 'The mental load of dinner, lifted' is exactly my phrase, then it's $25 a month in 'messages' and zero words about kids who eat twelve foods.

dd_offer.why: It says no card over and over, and the pricing box spells out that you just go back to Free after 14 days
dd_offer.expect_day_15: I lose the kid-safe profiles, the voting texts and the Kroger push and drop to the free plan unless I put a card in. Nothing gets charged.

head_to_head.reason: It's the only one that names kid-safe foods per person and says 'one safe thing on every plate', which is my OT's actual instruction

EM.reason: eMeals promises picky kids will 'love' it; DinnerDrop at least gives each person a won't-eat list

PTE.reason: Plan to Eat organizes recipes but I'd still be doing every safe-food decision myself

OL.reason: Ollie has the right vibe but a confusing $25 message plan and no per-person profiles

HF.reason: HelloFresh is sauced, mixed-texture boxes I can't make safe for Jalen

dd_fix_that_would_move_me: Home page sample week: replace 'Creamy Tomato Pasta with Hidden Veggies' and right under it show a real per-person profile screen (won't-eats, kid-safe foods) plus one line that exact brands stay in the cart unless you swap them.
